title: Bourbon Basics
subtitle: What the words on the label mean
description: A first tasting night for people who are new to bourbon. Four bourbons, lowest proof first, and each one carries a word from its own label that has a federal rule behind it: bourbon, bonded, straight with an age, and barrel proof. Along the way: how to taste, why wheat and rye change the glass, what was sold as bourbon before the rules, the 1897 Bottled-in-Bond Act, President Taft's 1909 decision, what the barrel does, and which words on a label have no rule at all.
tags: bourbon, beginner, american whiskey, labels, bottled in bond, straight bourbon, barrel proof, wheated bourbon, history

pours.name: Maker's Mark
pours.style: Kentucky straight bourbon whisky; 70% corn, 16% soft red winter wheat, 14% malted barley (the maker's figures)
pours.notes: Poured on slide 2. The word it teaches is bourbon, and it is the wheat half of the wheat and rye comparison.

pours.name: Old Grand-Dad Bonded
pours.origin: James B. Beam Distilling Co., Kentucky
pours.style: Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey, bottled in bond; the label says High Rye Mash Bill
pours.notes: The word it teaches is bonded. Taste it beside glass 1 for rye against wheat.

pours.name: Knob Creek 9 Year
pours.origin: James B. Beam Distilling Co., Clermont, Kentucky
pours.style: Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey, aged nine years
pours.notes: The words it teaches are straight and the age statement. Same proof as glass 2, so the difference is the recipe and the years.

pours.name: Wild Turkey Rare Breed
pours.style: Kentucky straight bourbon whiskey, barrel proof; no age statement
pours.notes: The words it teaches are barrel proof. Taste it neat, then with a few drops of water.
